title: Pocket Locks — Ask why the downhill reply can still spend water
summary: Questions about the water you leave
lead: These questions concern the puzzle’s fill tokens, not a real canal’s water volume. A gate name refers to a side of a chamber; that side need not always be physically lower.

questions.title: Can the downhill boat need a fill?
questions.prompt: Compare Unprepared return with Ready for descent. Both start at Reach 3, visit Reach 1 and return. Look at the chambers before the first sail.
questions.answer: Yes. A boat above a low chamber cannot enter until that chamber is brought to the boat’s level. The unprepared down-and-back route needs four fills; preparing both chambers in advance reduces it to two. Descending is not a promise that all the necessary water is already waiting.

questions.title: Does a taller lift spend more tokens?
questions.prompt: Compare the two rises in The tall middle hill. One rises by one level and the other by three. Keep your eye on fills, not just on the silhouette.
questions.answer: Each upward change spends one token in this puzzle. Its height does not multiply that price. The toy counts fill operations, not the volume of water or the energy of a real lock.

questions.title: Is arrival enough to finish?
questions.prompt: Try Down through the valley. When the boat reaches its destination, leave the last gate open for a moment and read the mooring instruction.
questions.answer: Not on this journey. Every gate must be shut at the finish. On Across the valley and back, gates must also be shut at the far-bank stop before the return begins. Sailing to a place and making a safe mooring are separate parts of the trip.

questions.title: Can full be the wrong starting level?
questions.prompt: Start a journey above a descent, with both chambers initially full. Compare each chamber with the reach where the boat must enter next.
questions.answer: Yes. Full means the higher physical level of that chamber, not ready for every approach. If the boat approaches from a lower reach, the chamber must be lowered for entry. The gate side names do not by themselves tell you which side is higher.

questions.title: Can an intermediate stop leave work for the return?
questions.prompt: At a journey that requires shut gates at its far-bank stop, close them all and inspect the chamber levels before sailing home.
questions.answer: Closing gates does not reset the water. The return inherits the levels left by the outward trip. A stop changes what the boat must do next, not the rule for filling or draining.

questions.title: Does Undo mean starting again?
questions.prompt: Make one legal gate or water action, then use Undo. Compare the boat and every chamber with the preceding position.
questions.answer: Undo restores the preceding accepted action, including its fill count and gate state. Restart restores the chosen journey from its original preparation. Those are different destinations in the puzzle, even when a first action makes them happen to coincide.
